statement: tests/test_expiry.py::test_token_expires fails intermittently. Make it pass reliably by fixing the underlying problem.

notes.goal: Make tests/test_expiry.py::test_token_expires pass reliably (fix the root cause).
constraint: No retry/skip/sleep workarounds in the tests: the user wants the root cause fixed.
rejected: Retrying the test (a @retry decorator was added to the test file): it only masks the bug; remove it.
hypothesis: Root cause confirmed: is_expired truncates `now` and `issued_at` to ints separately, so when the fractional parts straddle a second boundary the elapsed time is under-counted (e.g. issued 100.9, now 110.95 -> 10, not > 10).
next: Change syncer/expiry.py is_expired to compare `now - issued_at > ttl` on the floats, and delete the retry decorator from tests/test_expiry.py.

summary: The previous session traced the flaky test to is_expired in syncer/expiry.py: it truncates now and issued_at to ints separately, so elapsed time is under-counted when the fractional parts straddle a second boundary. It tried wrapping the test in a retry decorator (now in tests/test_expiry.py) but the user rejected retries as masking the bug. Fix: compare floats directly and remove the decorator.
